definition.simple: The dark, rich soil made from dead leaves and plants that acts like food for the forest.
definition.academic: The dark organic material in soils, produced by the decomposition of vegetable or animal matter and essential to the fertility of the earth.

examples: The forest floor is covered with a thick layer of humus that helps new seeds grow.
Worms and fungi help turn dead leaves into humus.

common_misconceptions: Students often confuse humus with 'hummus' (the food) or just normal sand/dirt. Humus is specifically organic and full of nutrients.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what happens to all the leaves that fall off the trees every year. Where do they go?
